requirement: Write a Bounded data descriptor that range-checks every assignment inclusively, names its attribute in error messages via __set_name__, stores each value on the owning instance under its own slot, returns itself on class access, and rejects inverted bounds, then use it for a Thermostat.
skeleton: Bounded descriptor with __init__ validating bounds, __set_name__ recording the name and a private slot, overloaded __get__ returning self for class access or the instance's slot value, and __set__ checking the range before setattr; Thermostat with two Bounded class attributes assigned in __init__.
caption: A range-checked attribute written as a Python data descriptor. Bounded(low, high) raises ValueError saying low must not exceed high for inverted bounds. __set_name__ receives the owner class and the attribute name when the class body is created, remembering the name for messages and a private slot _name for storage, so two descriptors on one class never share storage. __get__ is declared with typing.overload: accessed on the class, where instance is None, it returns the descriptor itself typed as typing.Self; accessed on an instance it returns getattr of the slot on that instance. __set__ raises ValueError saying the name must be between low and high unless low <= value <= high, then stores the value with setattr on the instance, never on the descriptor, which is shared by every instance. Thermostat declares target = Bounded(5, 30) and humidity = Bounded(0, 100) and assigns both in __init__, so construction is validated too. The fixture asserts that two thermostats keep independent values, that assigning 31 raises ValueError naming target and leaves 25 in place, that 5 and 100 are accepted while 100.5 raises ValueError naming humidity, that Thermostat.target is the Bounded with its limits, and that Bounded(10, 1) raises ValueError.

plan.intent: Validate numeric settings on every assignment
constraints: Each instance keeps its own values
Each attribute has its own storage
Limits are inclusive and violations raise ValueError naming the attribute
Accessing the attribute on the class returns the descriptor

rationale.teaches: A data descriptor using __set_name__ for naming and per-instance storage, with __get__ returning self when instance is None.
rationale.why: Storing on the descriptor or in a fixed slot works with a single instance and a single attribute, so the bug only shows when a second instance or second descriptor exists.

ops.docstring: Range-checked attributes through a descriptor that learns its own name.

ops.source:
class Thermostat:
    """A thermostat whose settings are range-checked on every assignment."""

    target = Bounded(5, 30)
    humidity = Bounded(0, 100)

    def __init__(self, target: float, humidity: float = 40) -> None:
        self.target = target
        self.humidity = humidity

candidates.why_wrong: Values are stored on the shared descriptor, so every instance sees the last value assigned anywhere.
Every descriptor uses the same storage slot, so setting humidity overwrites target.
Strict comparisons reject the documented inclusive limits such as 5 and 100.
Class-level access reads the slot from None and raises AttributeError instead of returning the descriptor.
Inverted bounds are accepted and create an attribute that can never be assigned.
